title: Cost, latency and the limits of an agent in production

videos.script: An agent is a loop, and every turn of the loop is a request that is paid for and waited for. This lesson measures one run of Marginalia's support agent on a local model: two requests, the tokens each one carried, and where the nineteen seconds went. {{title}} Most of every request was the same text, and the first request spent most of its time reading it. {{where}} A smaller model was faster, and broke on its very first tool call. Reusing a prefix saved the reading, until something at the front of the prompt changed on every request. {{levers}} Then the limits. An answer cut off at max tokens. A prompt too long for the window, cut without a word. And an overloaded server that the SDK retried twice before giving up. {{limits}} And how to put a budget in the code, so a run stops before it costs more than it is worth. {{last}}
